title: Docs: KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 fields + interpreting hit-rate (with troubleshooting)
author: Wei Chen
description: Summary: This PR documents Redwood’s KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 fields and provides guidance on how to interpret cache hit-rate in production. It includes a troubleshooting section aimed at Support/Solutions and customers who are comparing “hit-rate” vs observed latency/cost outcomes. This is intended to be consistent with the v2 metric spec + cardinality rules landing in runtime/platform work for the cache hit-rate instrumentation sprint. Motivation: We have multiple reports (incl. SUP-3921) that cache “hit-rate” is confusing without clear definitions of (a) what counts as a hit vs partial-hit, (b) how the metric is computed in streaming/retry scenarios, and (c) which breakdown dimensions are supported without tag explosion. This doc is also a prerequisite for Optimize’s “increase hit-rate” recommendations MVP to cite canonical definitions and to avoid teams implementing their own ad-hoc interpretations. Audience: External (customers using Hosted/Dedicated; with notes for Private) + internal (SRE/Support/SE). What’s included: (1) Definitions: hit, miss, partial-hit; difference between request-level and token/byte-level measurements; when a request is “cacheable.” (2) Field reference: stable metric names and primary tags/dimensions customers can use (tenant/route/model/version/region/deployment_mode), including which values are hashed/normalized. (3) “How to read dashboards”: examples for hit-rate vs hit-bytes vs saved_prefill_ms, and why hit-rate can drop while saved_prefill_ms stays flat (or vice versa). (4) Troubleshooting: missing metrics, unexpected hit-rate drops, tag explosion symptoms, and known edge cases (streaming retries / partial-prefill accounting / multi-route fragmentation) with mitigation steps. (5) Rollout notes: feature flags, staged enablement expectations, and data-quality caveats during rollout/backfill. Metric/field highlights (doc content): - redwood.cache.kv.lookup_total (counter): number of cache lookups attempted. - redwood.cache.kv.lookup_hit_total (counter): lookups resulting in full hit. - redwood.cache.kv.lookup_partial_total (counter): lookups resulting in partial hit (prefix overlap but not full prefill coverage). - redwood.cache.kv.lookup_miss_total (counter): lookup attempts with no usable cached prefix. - redwood.cache.kv.hit_bytes_total (counter): bytes of KV retrieved from cache (used for “hit-bytes”). - redwood.cache.kv.saved_prefill_ms_total (counter): estimated prefill compute time avoided due to cache hit/partial hit (see estimation caveats). - redwood.cache.kv.cacheable_prompt_total (counter): prompts meeting cacheability criteria at the gateway/runtime boundary (used for “cacheable prompt ratio”). Required/primary dimensions described in the doc (subject to v2 cardinality budget): - deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private - region: Redwood region identifier (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1) - route_id: stable route identifier (NOT raw path; normalized) - model: Redwood model slug (e.g., llama-3.1-70b-instruct) - model_version: semver/build id when pinned; otherwise “auto” or resolved version id (as documented) - tenant: internal tenant id; for external docs this is described as “workspace_id / project_id” depending on product surface. Notably excluded/explicitly discouraged: request_id in metrics (use tracing logs/events instead), raw prompt prefixes, unbounded user_id/session_id tags. Interpretations & formulas (documented): - Hit-rate (lookup-based): lookup_hit_total / lookup_total. - Effective hit-rate (including partial hits): (lookup_hit_total + w*lookup_partial_total) / lookup_total, where w is a configurable weighting; the doc cautions that dashboard defaults may differ by view. - Cacheable prompt ratio: cacheable_prompt_total / request_total (where request_total is the denominator for the same slice). - Saved prefill ms is not strictly proportional to hit-rate: it depends on prompt length distribution, model, hardware, and whether the cache hit is partial vs full. Troubleshooting checklist highlights: - “Hit-rate is high but p95 latency didn’t move”: verify that latency is dominated by decode, check that saved_prefill_ms_total is non-zero, check routing fragmentation (route/model/version pinned inconsistently), validate that you’re looking at cacheable prompts only. - “Hit-rate dropped after rollout”: check whether cache telemetry v2 is partially enabled (mixed v1/v2), check whether route_id normalization changed, check if model_version became unpinned/auto leading to fragmentation, check sampling settings and cardinality guardrails dropping high-cardinality slices. - “Metrics missing in Private”: confirm feature flag is enabled in the private control plane, confirm gateway attribution fields are present, verify metrics pipeline connectivity (doc includes Private-specific note to consult admin logs). References/links included in the docs: - Confluence: KV cache telemetry v2 metric spec; ADR-027 cardinality budget; data quality runbook; alerting proposal. - Linear: ENG-4820 (Docs + enablement), ENG-4812 (umbrella). - Related PRs: runtime instrumentation + gateway attribution + observability-pack dashboards (linked for internal readers). Screenshots/Examples: Added a small “example dashboard read” section using redacted sample numbers (no customer data). Notes: I intentionally avoided publishing internal-only metric names that are still in flux behind the feature flag; the doc uses the stable v2 names agreed in the spec and calls out “during rollout you may see both v1 and v2 panels” for a short period. Test plan: - Local docs build: yarn build (ok) - Link check: yarn test:links (ok) - Verified the external-facing pages render in staging with the nav entry under Observability > Caching. Rollout: Once merged, this will be referenced in the Console “?” tooltips and in Support macro drafts for SUP-3921 and related tickets.

(2) On partial hits: clarify that lookup_partial_total includes cases where we reuse some prefix but still run prefill for the remainder.
